text.arabic_uthmani: ذَٰلِكَ مِنْ أَنۢبَآءِ ٱلْغَيْبِ نُوحِيهِ إِلَيْكَ ۖ وَمَا كُنتَ لَدَيْهِمْ إِذْ أَجْمَعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَهُمْ وَهُمْ يَمْكُرُونَ

words.gloss_range: distal demonstrative compressing the completed Yusuf narrative into a single report-object
words.prose: {{ar:ذَلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhālika}}) turns the completed Yusuf narrative into one grammatical subject and holds it at a reverent distance. The first word therefore shifts the listener from the story world into a certification frame: that whole narrated arc is now the thing classified as unseen report and carried forward as revelation.

topics.headline: retrospective pointer to the whole story
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins by packaging the entire preceding narrative as one object of knowledge, not by continuing the plot.
topics.reason: The QAC demonstrative and attachment evidence support the word as the nominal starting subject, while the CRITICAL rows converge on retrospective compression and boundary shift.

words.gloss_range: partitive and source preposition assigning the prior story to the class of unseen reports
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) makes the prior story a member of a larger class and also lets it come from that hidden domain. The small preposition is the classificatory hinge: the narrative is not merely remembered, it is assigned to the category of unseen reports.

topics.headline: partitive source classification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the completed story reclassified as one instance from a wider unseen-news category.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the report noun as predicate complement, and the CRITICAL rows coherently preserve partitive, source, and boundary-bridge payoff.

words.gloss_range: plural construct report noun; weighty tidings from the unseen rather than routine narration
words.root_gloss_range: reporting, informing, consequential news, and prophetic news-bearing; here selected as plural unseen reports
words.prose: {{ar:أَنْبَاءِ}} ({{tr:anbāʾi}}) is the plural construct head of the phrase, so the story enters a recognized class of weighty reports bound to the unseen. Its root field keeps report-bearing and prophetic disclosure audible, while repeated formulas at 11:49 and 3:44 show that this is a credential pattern for histories the Prophet could not witness. The same report root also recalls Joseph’s promised disclosure at 12:15, now reframed as revelation to the Prophet.

topics.headline: unseen-report credential formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the noun as the core of a formula that authenticates inaccessible sacred history.
topics.reason: Construct grammar binds the noun to the unseen qualifier, and the inter-ayah rows explicitly tie the phrase to 11:49 and 3:44.

topics.headline: weighty plural report noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears this as consequential tidings in a plural report class, not as ordinary story information.
topics.reason: The lexical rows distinguish weighty report from routine report, while the plural and hamzated form keep the report-root visibly and audibly active.

topics.headline: report-root echoes across disclosure scenes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the root links internal narrative disclosure at 12:15 with the Prophet’s received report in 12:102.
topics.reason: The rows give concrete references for the same root field and do not force a different local sense.

words.gloss_range: definite gerund naming the inaccessible unseen domain that qualifies the reports
words.root_gloss_range: absence, hiddenness, concealment, and what is beyond perception or knowledge; here the epistemic unseen
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْغَيْبِ}} ({{tr:al-ghaybi}}) makes hiddenness the defining genitive domain of the reports. Its definite gerund form presents one known field of inaccessible knowledge, not scattered secrets, and that hiddenness becomes the premise for the proof that follows: the Prophet was not with them. Surah-local echoes from 12:10 and 12:81 move the root from physical concealment and human limitation into this final epistemic category.

topics.headline: definite unseen domain in construct
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the reports as belonging to a recognized unseen domain rather than to ordinary past memory.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make the word the genitive qualifier of the report noun; CRITICAL rows support definiteness, singularity, and gerund force.

topics.headline: hiddenness set against non-presence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the later absence clause matters: hidden content plus no witness route creates the proof logic.
topics.reason: The local sequence puts the hidden domain before the revelation verb and the denied presence clause, matching the CRITICAL proof-logic rows.

topics.headline: local and cross-surah unseen field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word gathers earlier hiddenness in Surah 12 and the repeated unseen-report formulas at 11:49 and 3:44.
topics.reason: The cited rows provide concrete references and preserve the same hidden-knowledge field without overriding the local genitive role.

words.gloss_range: Form IV imperfect revelation verb with divine subject, story object, and directed recipient frame
words.root_gloss_range: covert directed communication, signaling, inspiration, and divine revelation; here divine transmission of the prior story

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: accepted recitational contrast shifting the revelation verb to third-person singular while preserving transitive revelation grammar

words.prose: {{ar:نُوحِيهِ}} ({{tr:nūḥīhi}}) is the ayah’s transmission hub: the divine plural subject reveals the compressed story-object toward the addressed Prophet. The Form IV imperfect keeps revelation active and directed, answering the hiddenness just named and the non-presence about to be denied. Accepted variant evidence with {{ar:يُوحِيهِ}} ({{tr:yūḥīhi}}) preserves the same transitive revelation grammar while shifting the speaker stance from direct divine “We” to third-person “He.” The word also completes the unseen-report formula shared with 11:49 and 3:44 and echoes the surah’s revelation frame at 12:3 and 12:109.

topics.headline: divine transmission of the story-object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees exactly how hidden report becomes knowable: a divine subject sends the prior story-object to a prophetic recipient.
topics.reason: The suffix, verb agreement, and following recipient phrase are all supported by QAC and attachment evidence, and the CRITICAL rows converge on source-object-recipient structure.

topics.headline: Form IV directed revelation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears revelation as covert directed communication crossing hidden access, not as ordinary retelling.
topics.reason: V4 and CRITICAL lexical rows support the range of hidden directed signaling while the local Form IV and prophetic frame select divine revelation.

topics.headline: variant speaker-stance contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that accepted recitation evidence can shift grammatical speaker stance without changing the local revelation mechanism.
topics.reason: The canonical surface is first-person plural; the variant is retained as a recitational contrast, not allowed to replace the local displayed form.

topics.headline: unseen-report and surah revelation frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this verb as both the formula’s transmission verb and a closing certification of the surah’s revelation frame.
topics.reason: The rows cite 11:49, 3:44, 12:3, and 12:109 as concrete parallels for the same revelation pattern.

words.gloss_range: directional preposition plus second-person suffix marking the Prophet as revelation recipient
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَيْكَ}} ({{tr:ilayka}}) lands the revelation vector on the second-person addressee. The word fuses direction with address, so the Prophet is first marked as recipient and then, in the next clause, as the one who was not present at the hidden scene.

topics.headline: second-person revelation endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same addressee is both the endpoint of revelation and the non-witness of the event.
topics.reason: The preposition and suffix attach to the revelation verb and prepare the following second-person absence clause.

words.gloss_range: connector joining the revelation claim to the non-presence warrant
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) joins the revelation claim to the witness-absence clause. Its light connector form makes non-presence part of the same proof unit: the ayah moves from what is revealed to why revelation is the only route to knowing it.

topics.headline: connector from revelation to warrant
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the absence clause as evidence for the revelation claim, not as a detached biographical note.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence allows coordination or circumstantial force, and both readings preserve the CRITICAL payoff that the clauses form one proof unit.

words.gloss_range: past-negating particle scoping over the whole witness-absence clause
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) negates the whole past presence claim, not just a bare verb. With the perfect verb that follows, it states a categorical witness-route denial: the Prophet was not with them at the decisive scene.

topics.headline: categorical past non-presence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the proof depends on denying the entire past state of presence at the scene.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the particle as past negation before the perfect verb, and the CRITICAL rows preserve the scope and formulaic authentication payoff.

words.gloss_range: negated perfect second-person being, narrowed by the following locative to historical non-presence
words.root_gloss_range: being, becoming, existing, occurring, and serving as a state verb; here past locative presence denied
words.prose: {{ar:كُنْتَ}} ({{tr:kunta}}) makes the denied state a completed past fact and, with the following locative, narrows the root’s broad “being” range to historical presence at the scene. The second-person ending keeps the same addressee who received revelation inside the proof clause. The formula has concrete parallels in 3:44 and 28:44, where the Prophet’s absence from decisive hidden scenes likewise authenticates revealed knowledge.

topics.headline: past locative non-presence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the verb is not abstract existence here; it denies being at a specific historical scene.
topics.reason: The local complement selects locative presence, and the perfect under negation anchors the denial in completed past time.

topics.headline: prophetic witness-denial formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the clause as a standard authentication device for revealed access to unwitnessed events.
topics.reason: The rows cite 3:44, 11:49, and 28:44, and those echoes support formulaic witness denial without altering the local parse.

topics.headline: recipient becomes non-witness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the discourse role shift: the addressed recipient of revelation is placed outside the narrated scene.
topics.reason: The rows connect the verb to the surah’s address and boundary movement, and no guardrail evidence contradicts that discourse payoff.

words.gloss_range: locative adverb with third-person plural suffix denying co-presence with the conspirator group
words.prose: {{ar:لَدَيْهِمْ}} ({{tr:ladayhim}}) completes the absence claim as situational co-presence with them. The third-person suffix keeps the conspirator group compressed inside the adverb, and the following time clause narrows “with them” to the brothers at the exact resolution moment.

topics.headline: presence with the conspirators denied
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the denial is not general ignorance but absence from the precise setting where the plot was resolved.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the word the locative predicate of the negated state, and the temporal clause narrows the suffix’s practical referent to the conspirator group.

words.gloss_range: definite past-time particle narrowing the absence to the conspiracy moment
words.prose: {{ar:إِذْ}} ({{tr:idh}}) cuts the proof to a definite past moment: when they resolved their affair while scheming. It subordinates the conspiracy scene to the absence clause, so the ayah is not restarting the plot; it is locating the exact hidden event that revelation discloses.

topics.headline: definite past conspiracy moment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the proof zooming from general non-presence to the exact hidden moment under discussion.
topics.reason: The particle introduces a specific past temporal clause, and attachment evidence includes the nested circumstantial clause within its scene scope.

words.gloss_range: Form IV perfect plural: collective resolution of a plan, not mere physical gathering
words.root_gloss_range: gathering, collecting, bringing together, and Form IV resolving or agreeing; here unified conspiratorial decision
words.prose: {{ar:أَجْمَعُوا}} ({{tr:ajmaʿū}}) is Form IV, so the scene is not merely that they gathered; it is that multiple wills reached a completed resolution. The plural perfect carries the brothers as a collective subject, while the object that follows gives their resolution a bounded plan. The same rare form at 12:15 and the collocation echo with 10:71 make the final proof point back to the hidden decision that launched the human plot.

topics.headline: Form IV collective resolution
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word encodes deliberate consensus, not simple physical gathering.
topics.reason: QAC marks the Form IV perfect, and the CRITICAL rows distinguish the selected resolution sense from Form I gathering.

topics.headline: resolution at the center of the hidden scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the conspiracy as layered: formal resolution of a plan with an inner simultaneous scheming state.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the next word the object of the verb and the final clause circumstantial, matching the CRITICAL architecture rows.

topics.headline: rare resolution echo across plot scenes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the closing authentication verse answer the earlier hidden resolution at 12:15 and place it beside the adversarial formula of 10:71.
topics.reason: The cited echoes are concrete and preserve form/collocation payoff without controlling the local grammar.

words.gloss_range: singular possessed affair or plan as the object of collective resolution
words.root_gloss_range: command, affair, matter, directive, and plan; here their owned resolved plan with command pressure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: Form IV plural collective resolution immediately before the possessed plan noun
final imperfect plural scheming that completes the conspiracy field

words.prose: {{ar:أَمْرَهُمْ}} ({{tr:amrahum}}) supplies the resolved object: their singular possessed affair, plan, and directive. The singular noun with a plural suffix makes many agents hold one coherent objective, and the root’s command range gives the plan an adopted order-like force. Positioned between {{ar:أَجْمَعُوا}} ({{tr:ajmaʿū}}) and {{ar:يَمْكُرُونَ}} ({{tr:yamkurūn}}), it links formal consensus to continuing covert strategy, while Surah 12 echoes at 12:21 and 12:83 set this human plan against affairs that exceed human control.

topics.headline: one possessed plan-object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees many planners concentrated around one possessed objective, not scattered separate matters.
topics.reason: The word is the accusative object of the resolution verb, and the singular possessed form is central in the CRITICAL rows.

topics.headline: affair, plan, and directive force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the plan as more than a neutral matter: it has the force of an adopted directive.
topics.reason: The local collocation selects the resolved-plan sense while the root range preserves command pressure without replacing the local noun meaning.

topics.headline: plan network between resolution and scheming
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this noun as the hinge between collective resolution, ongoing scheming, and the surah’s wider contrast between human and divine affairs.
topics.reason: The cited co-occurrence and same-surah rows support the network payoff, including concrete references at 10:71, 12:21, 12:83, and 34:33.

words.gloss_range: circumstantial connector introducing simultaneous scheming, not a later sequence
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is the circumstantial connector before the final clause. It blocks a simple “then they plotted” sequence and makes the scheming simultaneous with the resolved plan, exposing the inner state that surrounded the outward act.

topics.headline: simultaneous circumstantial linkage
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the plotting as the state within the decision, not a later event after it.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the final clause as circumstantial, and the CRITICAL rows preserve simultaneity, nested linkage, and clause-pivot payoff.

words.gloss_range: independent third-person plural subject re-identifying the planners inside the circumstantial clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: singular possessed plan noun whose attached suffix is echoed by the independent subject pronoun

words.prose: {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) is retained even though the verb already marks a plural subject. The independent pronoun re-identifies the same planners as the schemers themselves and shifts from the attached suffix in {{ar:أَمْرَهُمْ}} ({{tr:amrahum}}) to explicit subjecthood in the circumstantial clause.

topics.headline: explicit same-agent subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices continuity of agency: the ones who possessed and resolved the plan are themselves the ones scheming.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the pronoun the subject of the final clause, and the CRITICAL rows support both grammatical completion and possession-to-subject pivot.

words.gloss_range: Form I imperfect plural scheming in a circumstantial clause, ongoing and objectless at the ayah close
words.root_gloss_range: covert planning, stratagem, hidden design, and trap-like maneuvering; here the brothers’ ongoing concealed plotting
words.prose: {{ar:يَمْكُرُونَ}} ({{tr:yamkurūn}}) leaves the ayah on an imperfect plural state: they are scheming while the plan is being resolved. The object is unstated, so the word characterizes their covert disposition while the narrative context supplies Joseph and the plan as understood targets. The root’s trap-like covert-planning image fits the ayah’s knowledge claim, because the hidden action is exactly what revelation exposes. Cross references such as 13:42, 14:46, 16:127, and 27:70 place human scheming under broader divine control and prophetic endurance formulas, while the final plural ending lets the ongoing group action carry the recitational close.

topics.headline: ongoing simultaneous scheming
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final action as a live hidden state inside the resolved act, not as a completed later plot.
topics.reason: The imperfect appears inside the circumstantial clause with an explicit plural subject, and the lack of object coherently characterizes the scheming state.

topics.headline: covert trap-like planning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears scheming as concealed strategy with moral color supplied by the local agents and target.
topics.reason: The lexical rows support covert planning and trap-like imagery while keeping moral valence locally determined rather than inherent in the root.

topics.headline: human plotting under wider divine control
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects this exposed past plot to wider Quranic patterns where human plotting is answered by divine control and prophetic endurance.
topics.reason: The rows cite 13:42, 14:46, 16:127, and 27:70, and those echoes add framing without changing the local imperfect ḥāl parse.

topics.headline: ongoing action at the recitational close
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah stops on the sound of ongoing plural scheming, matching the hidden state it discloses.
topics.reason: The form and phonetic rows support a closure payoff tied to the final imperfect ending and compact root texture.

baseline_models.mechanism: An incoming report supplies the payload, concealment blocks ordinary sight or knowledge, and a hidden imparting carries that payload to a recipient who did not share the event's time and place. Revelation functions as epistemic transport across non-presence.

strongest_changes: Revelation became a transport operation across non-presence, then the preceding scent, bearer, and restored sight sequence made that operation trace-like and perceptually restorative.
The private plot became coordinated consensus rather than isolated cunning, while the later majority and overlooked-sign sequence showed that agreement and prevalence can organize blindness.
The report became a disciplined route from concealed event to inspectable traces, outcomes, analogical crossing, and articulated guidance.
Retrospective fulfillment and hidden subtlety changed the disclosed object from a secret meeting alone into the latent order connecting scattered events.
summary.what_was_special: The focus verse contains two rival hidden circuits: coordinated human secrecy and hidden disclosure. The pericope repeatedly converts absence into mediated perception, private information into public reminder, apparent closure into delayed counter-arrival, and narrated past into a path for seeing and inference.
remaining_uncertainties: The transport and restored-sight analogy is structurally strong but does not prove that 12:94-96 defines revelation's mechanism.
The reading of subtlety as latent causal order competes with the simpler sense of benevolent kindness.
The critique of consensus is abductive because the later majority is not grammatically identified with the earlier council.
The ground-preparation, root-system, and scented-road models are deliberately contained branch activations and should not be presented as lexical translations.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Hidden news crosses absence through hidden imparting.** ن ب ء B002, غ ي ب B001, and و ح ي B001/B004 make revelation the transmission channel for an event inaccessible by presence. I infer that the listener’s non-presence is not a defect once news is supplied by this route.
2. **Concerted resolve becomes the concealed object later disclosed.** ج م ع B003 (concerted resolve) and ء م ر B001/B007 (affair; deliberation) return to the brothers’ gathering at 12:15. The ayah reads their hidden planning as exactly the kind of latent event revelation makes available.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:111 confirmed that this unseen report is not fabricated حديث but a detailed, confirming account.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Revelation bridging a scene inaccessible to ordinary witness.** `ن ب ء:B002` is consequential report or news, `غ ي ب:B001` is what is hidden from sight or knowledge, and `و ح ي:B004` is divine message or inspiration. The demonstrative recategorizes the foregoing account as unseen report, while the explicit denial of the addressee's presence at the brothers' collective plotting removes eyewitness access. The packet supplies both the inaccessible event and the named channel; I infer that revelation is assigned the evidentiary role that ordinary presence cannot perform. The ayah changes narrative detail from an implied observer's reconstruction into reported knowledge whose warrant is overtly identified.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:111 explicitly denies that the account is fabricated and assigns it confirmation and clarification, validating the unseen-report claim here through the final statement of narrative function.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak anlatımı, bir şeyin gerçekleşip bulunur hale gelmesini çekirdek kabul eder ve buna olma adları ile geçmiş ya da şimdiki bildirme kullanımlarını bağlar. Pekiştirme, ayırma ve ettirgen oluşturma kullanımları aynı dal içinde bağımlı kullanımlar olarak durur; yer, konum ve üstlenme dalları bu çekirdeğin yerine geçirilmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam hem yalın hem bağlı kullanımlar verdiği için tanım çekirdeği ayrı, bağlı sözleri ayrı tutar.

concept_map.definition: Bu dal, bir şeyin gerçekleşip bulunur hale gelmesini ve bu olmanın geçmiş ya da şimdiki anda bildirilmesini anlatır. Olma adları, pekiştirme ya da ayırma işlevli bağlı sözler ve bir şeyi oldurup oluşmasını sağlama buna bağlıdır.

facets.statement: Bir şeyin gerçekleşmesi, ortaya çıkması ve bulunur halde olması çekirdektir.
Olma ve oluş adları bu çekirdeğin adlaştırılmış biçimleridir.
Geçmişteki bir durumun haber verilmesi veya şimdiki olmanın bildirilmesi bu alana bağlıdır.
Pekiştirme ve gelen kişiyi kapsam dışı bırakma gibi bağlı söz dizimleri çekirdeğe ek kullanımlardır.
Bir şeyi oldurmak, onun gerçekleşmesini sağlama yönünde ettirgen bir uzantıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, dalı bir şeyin olması, gerçekleşmesi ve hazır bulunması etrafında toplar. Aynı bildirim içinde olma adları, geçmiş ya da şimdiki haber verme, pekiştirme, ayırma ve ettirgen oldurma kullanımları da bu çekirdeğe bağlanır.

root_mapping.policy: Use the dominant Furuq root for every QAC root, and include non-dominant Furuq targets as additional root_lexicon entries when qac-furuq-v4-root-map marks the QAC root as split.

root_lexicon.note: Turkish is the only language with dictionary entries/glosses currently sourced.
